text:
**Chase UK is the strongest pick specifically for everyday spending rewards, with Starling or Monzo better as all-round main accounts.**

There isn’t one universal “best” current account—it depends on whether you prioritise cashback, app tools, customer service, or other features. All the top options below are free (no monthly fee on the standard account), app-focused, FSCS-protected (up to £120,000), and support contactless/Apple Pay/Google Pay. Rates and offers change, so confirm the latest terms directly.

### Best for everyday spending cashback: Chase
Chase (part of JPMorgan) pays **2% cashback** on eligible UK debit or credit card spending in everyday categories—groceries/supermarkets, restaurants, cafes, takeaways, everyday transport (including TfL), fuel, and public EV charging—capped at **£20 a month** (up to £240 a year). 

- No monthly fee and no Chase fees on spending or cash withdrawals abroad (Mastercard rate).
- Qualification typically requires at least 15 payments a month (debit/credit card or Direct Debit) **and** £1,000+ held across Chase saver accounts every day of the previous month. New customers usually get a short grace period.
- Extras include spending insights, round-ups (with interest), and linked savers (including promotional rates for new customers and a regular saver).
- Drawbacks: App-only (no branches), no overdraft, and cashback is limited to those categories and UK/GBP spending. Cash deposits are limited.

Which? rates it a Recommended Provider, and MoneySavingExpert and comparison sites frequently highlight it for cashback on day-to-day card spending. It’s especially useful as a dedicated spending account (or second account) if you can meet the conditions.

### Best overall everyday experience: Starling or Monzo
These consistently rank at or near the top for customer satisfaction and app quality in Which? surveys and other reviews (Starling often leads customer scores; both are Which? Recommended Providers).

- **Starling**: Frequently praised as the best all-round free main account. Strong app with budgeting tools (Spaces), instant notifications, fee-free card spending and ATM withdrawals abroad (no practical monthly cap from the bank), overdraft options, and easier cash handling (e.g., Post Office deposits within limits). High customer service ratings, including phone support.
- **Monzo**: Excellent for hands-on budgeting—detailed spending categories and insights, Pots (for separating money), salary tools, round-ups, and instant notifications. Free tier covers fee-free card spending abroad (with ATM withdrawal limits outside the EEA); paid tiers add more features. Overdrafts available. Slightly more feature-rich for money management than the free alternatives for many users.

Independent surveys (including CMA/Ipsos service quality data) regularly put Monzo and Starling at or near the top for recommendation scores among personal current accounts.

### Quick comparison for everyday use
| Priority                  | Top pick     | Why |
|---------------------------|--------------|-----|
| Cashback on daily spends  | Chase       | 2% (capped) on groceries, eating out, transport, fuel |
| Smooth main account + travel | Starling | Top service scores, unlimited fee-free abroad, solid tools |
| Budgeting & control       | Monzo       | Best-in-class insights, Pots, notifications |
| Branches / traditional    | Nationwide or First Direct | Strong service scores; less app-focused rewards |

### Practical tips
- Many people run two accounts: e.g., Starling or Monzo as the main salary/bills account and Chase purely for eligible everyday card spending to earn the cashback.
- Check eligibility (usually 18+, UK resident, smartphone). Soft credit checks are common.
- High-street banks can still suit if you want branches or a switching bonus, but they generally lag the digital banks on app experience and ongoing spending rewards.
- Always read the current terms on the bank’s site before applying—cashback rules, saver rates, and limits can change.

For the latest side-by-side details, check MoneySavingExpert’s current account guides and Which?’s bank rankings, then compare the providers’ own pages.
